entries.name: Gygans
entries.description: Six-armed, one-eyed giants descended from an ancient cyclopean civilization that once spanned Thylea with grand city-states devoted to gaming competitions and to worshipping Sydon; their empire was exterminated by Pythor and the Dragonlords at the end of the First War, leaving only scattered, insular family groups.

entries.name: Keledone
entries.description: Golden, winged automata forged by the gods to resemble beautiful humanoids, tasked as eternally loyal guardians of temples and holy sites; their enchanting but deadly voices can lull victims to death or, conversely, offer comfort to the troubled.

entries.name: Maenad
entries.description: Once-human women transformed into frenzied fey servants of the gods and arch-fey of madness, lust, and pleasure through ritual, most often by cursed dryads like Demetria; they lure travelers into murderous bacchanals.

entries.name: Blemys
entries.description: Headless cyclopes with a single great eye set in their chest, considered the most intelligent (if antisocial) type of cyclops despite widespread assumptions of brainlessness; their fractured, curse-born civilization is of uncertain origin.

entries.name: Cerberus (Gloom Hounds)
entries.description: Three-headed hounds bred and tortured by hags to guard treasures and doorways with fanatical, ageless devotion; a slain cerberus's death dogs fight to the death for the right to grow a new head and become the new pack alpha.

entries.name: Bronze Automaton
entries.description: War constructs forged with mechanical precision and divine magic, singularly focused on combat and requiring periodic maintenance from skilled enchanters to remain functional over the years.

entries.name: Zephyr Dragon
entries.description: A little-known, gentler lesser kin of the metallic dragons, with wings fused to their forelimbs and shimmering bronze, brass, or copper scales; some scholars claim they predate true metallic dragons, a claim metallics dismiss as insulting.

entries.name: Nymph Subraces (Aurae, Naiad, Nereid, Oceanid, Oread)
entries.description: The five subraces of nymph fey tied to different domains — Aurae (sea and night sky islands), Naiads (fresh water, oracles and muses), Nereids (ocean coral reefs), Oceanids (coastal tricksters), and Oreads (mountains, reclusive and mischievous) — each embodying and protecting a different facet of Thylea's natural beauty.

entries.name: Troglodytes
entries.description: Foul, filthy-looking humanoids with chameleon skin that allows them to merge into walls. They are organized by strength and inhabit the Mithral Mines.
